new_entities.name: Finasteride treatment
new_entities.description: Finasteride used as a treatment for androgenetic alopecia.

new_entities.name: Androgenetic alopecia
aliases: male or female pattern hair loss
new_entities.description: Progressive androgen-mediated scalp hair loss in men or women.

edges.effect_quant: Pooled randomized evidence consistently shows that finasteride improves hair counts and patient-rated hair outcomes versus placebo in androgenetic alopecia.
edges.population: adults with androgenetic alopecia, especially men
edges.mechanism: Finasteride inhibits 5-alpha reductase, lowering dihydrotestosterone and reducing androgen-driven follicular miniaturization. That mechanism maps directly onto the condition biology, which is why finasteride tends to show clearer efficacy than many cosmetic or nutraceutical hair-loss interventions.
edges.summary: This is one of the stronger hair-regrowth treatment edges in the graph. Systematic reviews and network meta-analyses consistently place finasteride among the more effective evidence-based options for androgenetic alopecia, with benefits that are clinically real even if not universal or curative.
edges.caveats: The evidence is strongest for male-pattern hair loss and says less about women or atypical use patterns. Practical decision-making also has to weigh sexual and mood-related adverse-effect concerns, which sit outside the narrow efficacy question captured by this edge.
